title: Why Check?
lesson: Noise makes some results wrong. A check finds many of them and discards them.
brief: This circuit copies q0 onto q1. q0 starts at 0, so the correct result is always 00. The CNOT is noisy, so some runs come out wrong.
learning_moment: Without checks, noise turns some results into 01, 10 or 11. A check cannot fix those runs, but it can notice many of them and discard them. What is left is more often correct: that is Fidelity. You also keep fewer runs: that is Yield. This check asks whether q0 and q1 are still equal, so it catches a flip on one qubit; two flips at once (11) can still slip through.
hint: Drag a Z check onto q1 at slot 0, then drag its handle to slot 1. Verify it and test it under noise.
reflection: Which wrong results disappeared, and which one slipped through?
noise_note: The one CNOT is very noisy on purpose, so wrong results are easy to see.

noise.label: level noise with one very noisy CNOT (q0-q1)

par_note: No automated reference in this first puzzle: compare your layout with the circuit that has no checks.

explanation: Correct results are always 00, so q0 and q1 always agree.

A Z check started on q1 becomes Z on q0 and q1 after the CNOT. It ends at the last slot, so it uses the final readout to ask: are q0 and q1 still equal? Any run where only one of them flipped is discarded.
A flip on both qubits (11) keeps them equal, so that one slips through. That is why Fidelity rises but does not reach the top.
